summary: Woodford pressed consistent evidence, naturalistic alternatives, and inference gaps; Brierley defended cumulative Christian warrant through experience, explanation, morality, reason, and testimony.

pro.text: Conclusion, therefore Jesus is the son of God.
pro.context: Woodford provisionally grants two reported miracles to isolate the unsupported inference from remarkable events to Jesus's divine sonship.

con.text: his followers had experiences that they believed were of the risen Christ
con.context: Brierley includes reported appearances among several historical considerations offered as a cumulative resurrection case.

con-rational-belief-standard.words: Rational belief requires good reasons, yet reasonable people may evaluate evidence differently, so disagreement alone need not make either Christianity or atheism irrational.
con-rational-belief-standard.critique: Strongest feature: The argument establishes a moderate, clearly qualified standard that distinguishes rational disagreement from automatic irrationality while appropriately requiring participants to provide intelligible reasons for their beliefs. Principal limitation: Its description of reasons as personally valid remains epistemically underdeveloped, because personal acceptability, evidential adequacy, and truth-conduciveness are importantly different justificatory properties requiring differentiation. Live burden: The position must explain which publicly assessable criteria separate genuinely good reasons from sincere rationalizations without making unresolved disagreement itself disqualifying or merely subjective. Locked score: The strong or competent band reflects coherent calibration and useful framing, tempered by limited evidential development, terminological ambiguity, and only subsidiary contact with the central Christian warrant burden.

con-experience-and-investigation.words: An undefeated personal experience may rationally ground Christian belief, while objective investigation can provide additional intellectual support for Christianity.
con-experience-and-investigation.critique: Strongest feature: The move carefully presents experiential justification as defeasible rather than conclusive and explicitly distinguishes personally transformative experience from the separate availability of objective intellectual investigation. Principal limitation: It supplies no substantial procedure for assessing whether an experience is veridical, religiously specific, psychologically generated, or evidentially outweighed by conflicting experiences across incompatible traditions. Live burden: The experiential defense must identify credible defeaters and discrimination standards showing why trust remains warranted before independent corroboration, especially when similarly sincere reports support contradictory religious conclusions. Locked score: The strong or competent band recognizes precise qualification, coherent internal structure, and a defensible possibility claim, while withholding greater credit because the warrant remains autobiographical and comparatively undertested.

con-fine-tuning-intelligibility.words: Life-permitting fine-tuning and nature's mathematical intelligibility make better explanatory sense under purposive mind than as unguided coincidence.
con-fine-tuning-intelligibility.critique: Strongest feature: The argument combines life-permitting precision and mathematical intelligibility into a relevant comparative explanation, presenting purposive mentality as a coherent candidate rather than claiming deductive demonstration. Principal limitation: Its contrast largely reduces non-theistic possibilities to coincidence or luck, leaving physical necessity, observational selection, multiverse proposals, and impersonal structural explanations insufficiently compared. Live burden: The case must specify an explanatory metric and demonstrate that a divine mind predicts these observations better than serious alternatives without importing unexplained intentions or flexible post hoc purposes. Locked score: The strong or competent band reflects direct central-burden relevance, intelligible comparative structure, and restrained wording, moderated by compressed inference, incomplete rival testing, and comparatively limited evidential support.

con-dignity-and-moral-grounding.words: Christianity locates objective dignity and obligation in God's image and Christ's sacrifice, whereas material description alone cannot generate moral oughts.
con-dignity-and-moral-grounding.critique: Strongest feature: The move gives Christianity an intelligible internal account of exceptional human dignity by connecting divine creation, incarnation, and sacrifice directly with moral value and obligation. Principal limitation: It moves too quickly from bare material facts failing to yield oughts to atheism failing altogether, overlooking non-theistic realism, constructivism, naturalized normativity, and other irreducible possibilities. Live burden: The comparative claim must establish why divine commands, purposes, or valuations objectively ground dignity without circularity, while also showing that atheism itself entails none of the relevant moral resources. Locked score: The mixed band preserves substantial relevance and a recognizable Christian explanation, but reflects overstatement, unstable scope, insufficient engagement with alternatives, and limited support for the claimed comparative failure.

con-god-guarantor-of-reason.words: Wholly material causation allegedly undermines confidence in reasoning, whereas divine creation can make freedom and rational deliberation intelligible.
con-god-guarantor-of-reason.critique: Strongest feature: The argument directly addresses an important worldview-level question by offering divine creation as a unified explanation for freedom, rational responsiveness, and warranted confidence in deliberation. Principal limitation: It conflates causal determination with epistemic non-rationality and treats a divine guarantor as necessary without excluding compatibilism, reliable causal computation, evolutionary truth-tracking, or reasons-responsive mechanisms. Live burden: The case must show why materially realized reasoning cannot preserve logical relations and evidential sensitivity, then independently explain why divine creation reliably secures rather than merely permits cognitive accuracy. Locked score: The mixed band reflects high central relevance and a recognizable explanatory proposal, substantially constrained by equivocal terminology, an unsupported necessity claim, inadequate alternative testing, and weak representational charity.

con-resurrection-best-explanation.words: Crucifixion, an empty tomb, reported appearances, conversions, and early church growth are collectively presented as best explained by resurrection.
con-resurrection-best-explanation.critique: Strongest feature: The move identifies a concrete collection of historical explananda and organizes them into a straightforward cumulative inference aimed directly at Christianity's indispensable resurrection bridge. Principal limitation: Listing disputed facts does not establish their reliability, evidential independence, or comparative diagnosticity, and the excerpt does not seriously test grief experiences, legendary development, error, or social explanations. Live burden: The inference must defend each premise source-critically, account for dependence among reports, incorporate supernatural prior considerations, and compare resurrection against strong combinations of ordinary hypotheses. Locked score: The strong or competent band recognizes clarity, central relevance, and cumulative organization, while reflecting materially overstated comparative force, underdeveloped historical warrant, implicit qualifications, and limited treatment of alternatives.

pro-scientific-correction-of-genesis.words: Christian acceptance of evolution followed overwhelming scientific correction rather than clear Genesis foresight, weakening revelation as an independent guide to nature.
pro-scientific-correction-of-genesis.critique: Strongest feature: The reply supplies a concrete historical challenge to revelation's claimed explanatory independence by contrasting longstanding creation readings with Christianity's later accommodation to overwhelming evolutionary evidence. Principal limitation: Its broad claims about most Christians and Christianity being dragged toward correction require wider historical documentation and insufficiently acknowledge nonliteral or accommodationist interpretive traditions. Live burden: The criticism must show that representative doctrinal interpretation, rather than merely some literalist communities, systematically changed because external evidence exposed revelation's prior ambiguity or error. Locked score: The mixed band reflects a relevant and potentially forceful revelation objection with recognizable historical support, offset by sweeping scope, incomplete substantiation, and failure to answer the targeted fine-tuning comparison directly.

pro-consistent-evidence-trilemma.words: Standards permissive enough for Christianity also rationalize incompatible religions; stricter standards reject them, while Christianity-only standards require special justification.
pro-consistent-evidence-trilemma.critique: Strongest feature: The trilemma directly pressures both experiential permissiveness and general good-reasons language by demanding consistently applicable standards across mutually incompatible religions rather than denominational exemption. Principal limitation: Its supposedly exhaustive framing overstates the dilemma because epistemic permissibility can vary with individual evidence, and rationally holding incompatible conclusions across different persons creates no logical contradiction. Live burden: The argument must specify a common evidential baseline and show that relevantly similar cases receive asymmetrical treatment, without equating rational justification with truth or personal inconsistency. Locked score: The mixed band acknowledges sharp burden contact, memorable structure, and an important consistency challenge, while reflecting imprecise conditions, excessive exhaustiveness, and insufficient allowance for evidence-relative rational disagreement.

pro-divine-communication-objection.words: A loving, omnipotent God could communicate Christianity clearly, so unbelief, doctrinal disagreement, and unequal indirect transmission count against that God.
pro-divine-communication-objection.critique: Strongest feature: The objection derives a clear evidential expectation from divine power and love, then connects widespread disagreement and unequal informational access directly to Christianity's claimed revelation. Principal limitation: The expectation that a loving God would convince everyone remains too strong without examining other proposed purposes, freedom-related considerations, epistemic distance, moral development, or differentiated responsibility. Live burden: The argument must formulate a proportionate communication expectation that survives plausible divine-purpose replies while explaining why severe, apparently arbitrary disparities remain improbable under Christian theism. Locked score: The strong or competent band reflects direct responsiveness, substantial central relevance, and a powerful explanatory mismatch, tempered by insufficient qualification of love, conviction, universality, and the range of competing theological explanations.

pro-rationality-without-free-choice.words: Rationality concerns aligning beliefs and actions with reasons and evidence, not freely choosing which beliefs one happens to hold.
pro-rationality-without-free-choice.critique: Strongest feature: The reply cleanly separates voluntary belief selection from rational responsiveness, exposing why causal determination alone does not eliminate evidential relations, logical assessment, or reasons-guided conduct. Principal limitation: Defining rationality through correspondence with reasons and evidence does not itself establish that naturally produced cognition accurately identifies either, leaving a distinct reliability question unresolved. Live burden: The account must explain how determined cognitive mechanisms achieve dependable truth-tracking and error correction while preserving the conceptual distinction between causal explanation and epistemic justification. Locked score: The very strong band reflects a precise diagnostic defeat of the freedom premise, exceptional directness, stable terminology, and appropriately limited force, with remaining restraint because global cognitive reliability requires additional argument.

pro-naturalistic-moral-cooperation.words: Shared aversion to suffering, biological interests, and cooperative rules can sustain morality even without metaphysically ultimate wrongness.
pro-naturalistic-moral-cooperation.critique: Strongest feature: The response gives a concrete naturalistic pathway from shared vulnerability, suffering aversion, biological interests, and cooperation to workable moral rules while candidly conceding non-ultimate metaphysical status. Principal limitation: Its account shifts among preference, inherited disposition, collective advantage, and normativity without fully explaining how descriptive coordination yields authoritative obligations when interests conflict. Live burden: The position must distinguish practical social morality from objective moral truth and show how its proposed procedures adjudicate exploitation, minority protection, sacrifice, and disagreements beyond reciprocal advantage. Locked score: The strong or competent band recognizes responsive comparative force, explicit calibration, and a plausible naturalistic possibility, while reserving higher evaluation because metaphysical objectivity and the transition from interests to obligations remain unresolved.

pro-davids-child-moral-objection.words: The punishment of David through his innocent child's death conflicts with the existence of an omnipotent and omnibenevolent God.
pro-davids-child-moral-objection.critique: Strongest feature: The objection isolates a vivid scriptural case in which the child's death is expressly connected to David's wrongdoing, creating a direct challenge for Christian moral coherence. Principal limitation: Moving from grave moral tension to strict incompatibility requires additional premises concerning innocence, punishment, divine authority, afterlife compensation, narrative reliability, and permissible divine purposes. Live burden: The challenge must defend those moral premises while requiring a specific account of whether the event occurred, was divinely caused, was narratively misattributed, or can be justified. Locked score: The strong or competent band reflects substantial textual grounding, central relevance, and an unresolved punitive problem, moderated by the stronger logical-conflict formulation and assumptions about the narrative's precise causal interpretation.

con-christological-scripture-reading.words: Difficult Old Testament narratives are partial, culturally situated revelation interpreted through the fuller disclosure of God in Jesus.
con-christological-scripture-reading.critique: Strongest feature: The response offers a coherent Christ-centered interpretive framework that treats difficult narratives as partial and culturally situated rather than allowing every surface reading to define Christianity conclusively. Principal limitation: The framework does not resolve the cited child's death and leaves unspecified whether problematic descriptions record divine action, human misattribution, pedagogical accommodation, or morally justified conduct. Live burden: The method must provide nonselective interpretive criteria showing when Jesus corrects, reframes, or confirms earlier claims without simply protecting favored doctrine from counterevidence. Locked score: The strong or competent band recognizes direct contact, useful hermeneutical qualification, and proportionate defensive force, while reflecting incompleteness on the specific moral conflict and uncertainty about partial revelation's scope and authority.

pro-proportionate-supernatural-evidence.words: Extraordinary Christian claims require proportionate evidence, and transmitted testimony, apparent wonders, and potentially altered texts do not automatically satisfy that standard.
pro-proportionate-supernatural-evidence.critique: Strongest feature: The reply states a broadly applicable proportionality principle and connects evidential demand to claim type, directly challenging reliance on testimony and experience for extraordinary conclusions. Principal limitation: Its categorical dismissal of transmitted evidence outruns the selected development because testimony can vary considerably in independence, proximity, reliability, corroboration, and alternative-resistant explanatory power. Live burden: The case must operationalize proportionality through explicit comparisons among source quality, prior plausibility, dependence, expected error, and the cumulative probability of ordinary competing explanations. Locked score: The very strong band reflects central burden contact, principled consistency, clear calibration, and strong responsiveness, with limited restraint because source-specific historical analysis is needed to establish insufficiency rather than merely announce the governing standard.

pro-miracles-do-not-entail-divinity.words: Even granting virgin birth and resurrection provisionally, those events alone do not logically entail that Jesus is God's son.
pro-miracles-do-not-entail-divinity.critique: Strongest feature: The argument provisionally grants the disputed miracles and then precisely identifies the missing logical bridge from extraordinary birth or resurrection to Jesus's specific divine identity. Principal limitation: Its deductive diagnosis does not address whether those events, combined with Jesus's teachings, context, intentions, and antecedent theology, could provide substantial abductive evidence for sonship. Live burden: Christianity must supply independent identity premises and causal discrimination showing why God, rather than unknown agency or another supernatural explanation, authorized the events and vindicated the claimed conclusion. Locked score: The very strong band reflects exceptional precision, directness, charity, and decisive exposure of non-entailment, while remaining proportionate because defeating deduction alone does not eliminate every cumulative or probabilistic identity inference.

con-early-testimony-access.words: Textual criticism, early documents, eyewitness indications, and Pauline traditions provide substantial access to first-century Christian claims.
con-early-testimony-access.critique: Strongest feature: The reply identifies several historically relevant mechanisms for recovering early Christian claims, including documentary proximity, textual criticism, eyewitness indications, and traditions preserved within Pauline material. Principal limitation: Terms such as extremely close and eyewitness remain insufficiently specified, while early access alone does not establish independence, accurate transmission, authorship, or truth concerning miraculous events. Live burden: The defense must date and identify its sources, analyze literary dependence and divergence, distinguish testimony from later attribution, and explain what reliability threshold supports resurrection inference. Locked score: The strong or competent band recognizes coherent historical relevance, substantial contact with transmission concerns, and useful source categories, tempered by underdeveloped documentation and failure to answer the separate logical gap from reported miracles to divine identity.

con-fine-tuning-probability-qualified.words: Fine-tuning tolerance is not ordinary event probability, yet the life-permitting range's extreme precision still calls for explanation.
con-fine-tuning-probability-qualified.critique: Strongest feature: The response explicitly concedes that a constant's tolerance cannot straightforwardly be treated like repeated dice probability, thereby improving calibration while preserving a narrower explanatory question. Principal limitation: Although methodologically relevant, the qualification does not answer the targeted objection that Christian interpretation of nature historically followed external scientific correction rather than independent revelatory clarity. Live burden: The remaining design case must compare purposive agency with necessity, observational selection, and multiverse explanations without converting a narrow tolerance interval into an unsupported probability distribution. Locked score: The strong or competent band reflects intellectual concession, precise qualification, logical clarity, and continuing central relevance, offset by its status as an adjacent nonanswer to the assigned Genesis-and-revelation challenge.

con-evolutionary-truth-defeater.words: If evolution selects cognition mainly for survival rather than truth, naturalism allegedly lacks adequate grounds for trusting evolved beliefs.
con-evolutionary-truth-defeater.critique: Strongest feature: The reply directly reaches the naturalistic reliability question by asking whether survival-oriented selection can justify confidence in the beliefs and inferential processes it produces. Principal limitation: It opposes survival and truth too sharply, offering no demonstration that broadly accurate environmental representation lacks adaptive value or that evolved cognition is generally unreliable. Live burden: The defeater must estimate reliability under naturalism, distinguish abstract metaphysical belief from ordinary perception, and address social correction, prediction, replication, and domain-specific error detection. Locked score: The mixed band preserves high relevance and genuine responsiveness to the central trust issue, while reflecting materially overstated force, weak evidential support, insufficient qualification, and limited engagement with the strongest truth-tracking evolutionary alternative.

pro-fallible-cognition-and-verification.words: Evolved cognition remains uncertain but manageable through verification, and epistemic discomfort does not warrant choosing a more appealing theistic worldview.
pro-fallible-cognition-and-verification.critique: Strongest feature: The reply accepts cognitive fallibility rather than promising certainty, invokes verification as an error-management practice, and rejects any inference from epistemic discomfort to a preferred theistic conclusion. Principal limitation: Verification itself employs evolved cognition, and the excerpt provides no examples, success criteria, independence conditions, or explanation of how cross-checking answers a genuinely global defeater. Live burden: The account must describe prediction, replication, instrumental measurement, adversarial checking, and convergent correction sufficiently to show reliability improvement without presupposing comprehensive cognitive trust. Locked score: The strong or competent band reflects excellent direct responsiveness, stable qualification, and coherent fallibilism, moderated by limited evidential development and its subsidiary rather than complete contribution to naturalistic epistemology.

strengths: Woodford repeatedly applied a common proportionality standard to Christian and non-Christian supernatural claims, placing the central evidential burden clearly in view.
His distinction between rational responsiveness and voluntary belief choice directly dismantled the argument that determined cognition is automatically non-rational.
The provisional grant of virgin birth and resurrection exposed a specific missing inference from remarkable events to Jesus's divine identity.
His naturalistic accounts of cooperation and fallible verification supplied constructive alternatives rather than relying exclusively on criticism.
The scriptural case involving David's child created a concrete unresolved challenge for the claimed moral coherence of omnibenevolent governance.

blunders.text: The Genesis reply addressed revelation's historical ambiguity but did not answer the targeted comparative inference from fine-tuning and mathematical intelligibility.
The evidence trilemma was framed too exhaustively and blurred the distinction between incompatible truths and evidence-relative rational permission.
Several strong objections needed fuller positive models, particularly the mechanisms by which verification earns trust and naturalistic interests become obligations.

strengths: Brierley began with a moderate account of rational disagreement that avoided treating atheism as irrational merely because Christianity was defended.
His cumulative case covered cosmic order, dignity, reason, experience, testimony, and resurrection, giving the Christian route broad explanatory reach.
The fine-tuning probability concession materially improved precision by separating physical tolerance from ordinary repeated-event probability.
His early-testimony reply directly engaged transmission concerns through textual criticism, documentary proximity, and early Pauline traditions.
The Christ-centered reading of difficult scripture offered a proportionate interpretive defense rather than claiming every troubling passage had been solved.

blunders.text: The reason argument treated material causation as non-rational and asserted divine guarantee as necessary without eliminating compatibilist or truth-tracking alternatives.
The morality case generalized from material facts to atheism broadly, leaving non-theistic realism and other moral ontologies substantially unaddressed.
The resurrection case listed its explananda without sufficiently defending their independence, reliability, or superiority over serious ordinary combinations.
The evolutionary defeater relied on an insufficiently defended opposition between survival value and accurate representation.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that Christianity lacks proportionate public warrant when its distinctive supernatural conclusions depend on contested testimony, uneven revelation, and explanatory inferences that remain underdetermined by their evidence.

novelty.explanation: This integrates three transcript objections into a single proportionate thesis without attributing the synthesis to Woodford.

premises.text: Extraordinary causal and identity claims should receive lower initial confidence and require evidence whose independence, reliability, and discriminatory power increase with the claim's departure from well-established experience.

novelty.explanation: This develops the proportionality standard by specifying independence, reliability, and discriminatory power.

premises.text: Early access to Christian claims can establish what communities reported without by itself establishing independent eyewitness confirmation, accurate supernatural interpretation, or the truth of the reported events.

novelty.explanation: This repairs an overly categorical treatment of testimony by conceding historical access while limiting its inferential reach.

premises.text: Even well-supported anomalous events would leave their cause and theological meaning underdetermined unless additional evidence identified the responsible agency and connected that agency to specifically Christian doctrine.

novelty.explanation: This extends the non-entailment diagnosis into a broader causal and theological underdetermination principle.

premises.text: A perfectly loving and capable revealer would reasonably be expected to reduce severe, morally consequential disparities in sincere access more effectively than the observed pattern of ambiguity and inherited disagreement suggests.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the universal-conviction claim by using a qualified expectation about severe access disparities.

premises.text: Naturalistic accounts need not guarantee infallibility; prediction, replication, independent instrumentation, and adversarial correction can justify domain-specific confidence while leaving every worldview open to revision.

novelty.explanation: This supplies mechanisms missing from the transcript's brief appeal to verification and fallibilism.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, withholding belief from Christianity's distinctive supernatural and identity claims can be rational when the available evidence does not sufficiently discriminate those claims from serious historical, psychological, and theological alternatives.

novelty.explanation: This draws a limited withholding conclusion rather than claiming that every form of Christian belief is demonstrably false.

newArguments.title: The transmission bottleneck argument
newArguments.text: If a universally consequential revelation is routed mainly through ancient languages, disputed authorship, manuscript reconstruction, institutional inheritance, and uneven missionary history, those bottlenecks are not merely accidental background conditions. They become observations to compare against rival hypotheses about the revealer's aims. A human cultural-development hypothesis readily predicts geographical clustering, doctrinal branching, and dependence on inherited testimony. A perfectly capable communicator hypothesis needs additional reasons for expecting the same pattern. This comparison strengthens the hiddenness objection without assuming that love requires coercive certainty or identical experiences for every person.

novelty.explanation: This newly frames transmission structure itself as comparative evidence rather than restating any participant's direct argument.

newArguments.title: Causal underdetermination after anomaly
newArguments.text: Suppose several resurrection-related facts were granted at unusually high confidence. The inference would still require two stages: first, identifying resurrection rather than misperception, survival, legend, or unknown intervention; second, identifying the agent's theological meaning. Evidence adequate for an anomaly may remain inadequate for divine sonship, scriptural authority, or an entire doctrinal system. Separating event, cause, and interpretation prevents confidence gained at one stage from being silently transferred to later conclusions. It also explains why cumulative evidence must be evaluated for discrimination, not merely accumulated as a larger list.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's entailment gap into a staged model of event, cause, and theological interpretation.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that Christianity can be rationally held as a defeasible cumulative explanation when experiential, philosophical, moral, and historical considerations jointly raise its plausibility without requiring certainty.

novelty.explanation: This repairs overstatement by presenting the Christian case as cumulative, defeasible, and explicitly short of certainty.

premises.text: Rational commitment can be comparative and graded: a person may reasonably prefer the worldview that best integrates several evidence classes even when each consideration is individually contestable.

novelty.explanation: This develops the transcript's moderate rationality standard into an explicit cumulative and comparative model.

premises.text: Fine-tuning and mathematical intelligibility need not establish a numerical design probability to count as evidence if purposive mentality makes a life-permitting, discoverable order less surprising than specified rival hypotheses do.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the design inference by abandoning unsupported ordinary probability language and requiring explicit rival comparison.

premises.text: Christian moral anthropology offers an internally unified account of equal dignity, obligation, forgiveness, and sacrificial concern, although its comparative success must be assessed against serious non-theistic moral realism.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the positive Christian account while withdrawing the unsupported assertion that atheism cannot ground value.

premises.text: Historical evidence can rationally support resurrection only after source dependence, dating, genre, alternative explanations, and background plausibility are openly incorporated rather than bypassed by listing traditional facts.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the historical case by adding the comparative and source-critical work identified as missing.

premises.text: Religious experience can provide defeasible first-person justification when it coheres with other evidence, produces no contradiction, and remains responsive to psychological, moral, and evidential defeaters.

novelty.explanation: This adds discrimination and defeater conditions to the transcript's otherwise underspecified experiential justification.

conclusion.text: Therefore Christianity may be rational for a believer when this cumulative case survives serious alternative comparison and identified defeaters, even though the same evidence need not rationally compel every informed evaluator.

novelty.explanation: This gives the cumulative case a modest rational-permissibility conclusion consistent with persistent reasonable disagreement.

newArguments.title: Cross-domain coherence without simple addition
newArguments.text: A cumulative case should not treat every consideration as an independent vote. Instead, Christianity can claim support when one hypothesis jointly anticipates a discoverable cosmos, normatively significant persons, transformative experience, and a historically embedded revelation. Dependence and tension among these observations must be modeled openly, but explanatory integration can still matter: one framework may reduce the number of unrelated assumptions needed to connect them. The argument succeeds only comparatively, after rival naturalistic and religious packages receive equally charitable construction, and therefore supports rational preference rather than compulsory assent.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a disciplined coherence model that neither participant articulated, including controls for dependence and rival comparison.

newArguments.title: Costly correction as experiential evidence
newArguments.text: Religious experience is more evidentially interesting when it produces specific, costly, and independently observable correction rather than comfort or familiarity alone. A Christian could therefore narrow the experiential claim to cases involving durable restitution, relinquishment of advantage, reconciliation, or resistance to prior prejudice, while still allowing psychological explanations and counterexamples. Such outcomes would not prove divine causation, but they could modestly increase confidence when predicted by the tradition's moral center and integrated with other evidence. This approach reduces reliance on private resonance and makes at least part of the experiential case publicly assessable.

novelty.explanation: This newly proposes costly behavioral correction as a constrained, partially public test of experiential claims.
